title: Is This Code Mine? Student Ownership When AI Agents Write the Spec and the Code
abstract: arXiv:2611.21501v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Software engineering courses are starting to ask students to build entire systems with AI coding agents, but little is known about what students actually do with them and whether they still own what they deliver. If the agent writes both the code and the decisions behind it, the artifacts we grade no longer show what students learned. We studied an assignment in which 18 pairs of students built applications with agents under Spec-Driven Development, combining the mined history of their repositories, the prompts they recorded, and a survey of 33 students. The agents wrote 69\% of the specifications meant to keep students in control, sometimes from a prompt of a few words. Students locate their ownership in the ideas, crediting themselves with half of them but a fifth of the code, yet most could not explain that code to a colleague or modify it without the agent, and what they report having written is unrelated to what their own commits de

translated_title: 这段代码是我的吗？当AI智能体编写规范与代码时学生的成果所有权问题
translated_abstract: 软件工程课程开始要求学生使用AI编码智能体构建完整的系统，但学生实际上如何使用这些智能体，以及他们是否仍然拥有自己交付的成果，目前知之甚少。如果智能体既编写了代码，又做出了代码背后的决策，那么我们用来评分的作业成果就不再能反映学生究竟学到了什么。我们研究了一项作业任务，其中18组学生（两人一组）在规范驱动开发下与智能体协作构建应用程序，研究结合了对他们代码仓库历史的挖掘、他们记录的提示词，以及对33名学生的调查。结果显示，智能体编写了69%的、本应让学生保持掌控权的规范，有时仅凭几个词的提示就能完成。学生将自己的所有权定位于想法层面，认为自己贡献了一半的想法，但只有五分之一的代码；然而大多数人无法向同事解释这些代码，也无法在没有智能体的情况下修改代码，而且他们自述编写的内容与其提交记录所显示的情况并不相符。
tldr: 本研究通过对18组学生作业的实证分析发现，在规范驱动开发下AI智能体编写了69%的规范和绝大部分代码，学生虽主张对想法的所有权，但大多无法解释或独立修改代码，且其自述贡献与实际提交记录不符，揭示了AI时代编程作业中所有权与学习评估的深层问题。
en_tdlr: An empirical study of 18 student pairs using AI coding agents under Spec-Driven Development reveals that agents wrote 69% of the specifications and most of the code, students claimed ownership over ideas but largely could not explain or independently modify the code, and their self-reported contributions were unrelated to their actual commits.
